situation:
You are the foodservice manager at GRANITE ROW MARKETS, a chain of eleven convenience stores owned by the people who work in them. The general manager (judge), elected by the member-owners two years ago, has asked you to bring a recommendation on the crew meal and discount policy.

The hot-food program is the reason customers stop. Every store runs a full hot case of fried chicken, breakfast burritos and roller-grill items from five in the morning until close, and a case that looks full sells; a picked-over case does not. Painted on each front window is the line the co-operative was founded on: the people serving you own this store.

At the last members' meeting the crew voted themselves an open crew meal: any member-owner on shift may take food from the hot case free, at any hour. Nothing about that breaks a rule, since the crew own the food. But regular customers now watch employees take chicken from the same case they are paying for, and several have said so at the counter.

Holding the open crew meal keeps faith with the line painted on the front window and with the benefit the members voted for, and it leaves the hot case picked over through the dinner rush and leaves customers watching it happen. Limiting the free meal to food pulled after close, with a half-price discount during shift, protects the merchandised case and takes back a benefit the member-owners granted themselves.

Either way you will have to bring the member-owners with you, since they are the ones who voted. The general manager (judge) wants your recommendation on the crew meal and discount policy, and wants to hear how you would explain it to the customers at the counter. The general manager (judge) will greet you, ask to hear your ideas, and will thank you after your presentation and questions.
judgeCharacterization:
You are the general manager (judge) of GRANITE ROW MARKETS, elected by the member-owners two years ago. Business background is the same as the situation above. You know the hot case is what brings customers through the door, you were in the room when the members voted themselves the open crew meal, and you have heard the comments at the counter. You want the foodservice manager to recommend what the crew meal and discount policy should be, to say how the member-owners would be brought along, and to explain how it would be put to customers.

You will greet the participant, ask to hear their ideas, and listen to the presentation without steering it. After the presentation, ask the following questions:
judgeQuestions: Six months from now, how would we know this was the right call?
What would you be watching at the counter to tell you it is working?
